title: Peach Crisp with Buttery Almond Crumbs
summary: Juicy peaches in a buttery reduced syrup, topped with pre-toasted bread, almond and spice crumbs that stay crunchy.
equipment: 23 cm pie dish or 1.5-litre baking dish

ingredients.item: ripe peaches, peeled, stoned and cut in 1.5 cm wedges
fine sea salt or table salt
slices white sandwich bread, crusts on
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Macerate the peaches
steps.text: Toss the peaches with the sugar and salt and leave 30 minutes, then drain in the sieve, keeping the juice. Drawing out the juice first stops the crisp turning watery.

steps.title: Make the crumbs
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Pulse the bread, almonds, brown sugar, cold butter, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt in the food processor into coarse, buttery crumbs.

steps.title: Toast the crumbs
steps.text: Spread the crumbs on the baking tray and bake 10-15 minutes, stirring once, until golden and crisp. Pre-toasting means the topping stays crunchy on top of the soft fruit.

steps.title: Reduce the juice
steps.text: Boil the reserved peach juice with the 30 g butter in the frying pan until syrupy, about 3 minutes, then whisk in the lemon juice and cornflour and cook 30 seconds until thick.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Turn the drained peaches in the syrup, tip into the pie dish and bake 15-20 minutes until bubbling. Scatter the toasted crumbs over and bake 5 minutes more. Cool 15 minutes before serving.

tips: To peel peaches easily, score a cross, dip in boiling water for 30 seconds and slip off the skins.
A common mistake is skipping the draining step; the crisp becomes watery.
Toast the crumbs until properly golden; they will not brown further on the fruit.
Ripe but firm peaches give the best texture.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best on the day. Store leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 2 days, and keep extra crumbs in an airtight jar.
